request.user:
Subject: Zoology
Question type: single-correct (exactly one option is right)

Which of the following pairs of hormones are not antagonistic (having opposite effects) to each other?
(A) Parathormone – Calcitonin
(B) Insulin - Glucagon
(C) Aldosterone Atrial Natriuretic Factor
(D) Relaxin - Inhibin

result.working: Parathormone raises blood Ca2+ and calcitonin lowers it, so they are antagonistic. Insulin lowers blood glucose and glucagon raises it, so they are antagonistic. Aldosterone retains Na+ and water, raising BP, while ANF promotes Na+ excretion and vasodilation, lowering BP, so they are antagonistic. Relaxin softens the pubic symphysis and cervix during parturition, while inhibin inhibits FSH secretion. These are unrelated effects, so the pair is not antagonistic.
